description: Authentic reproduction of the 1911 Curtiss Pusher flown by John G. Kaminski Milwaukee's first pilot; built 1974 by Dale and Dean Crites of Waukesha using many parts from an original Curtiss Pusher; flown at airshows for 13 years for 44 hours total with a last flight at Wilmington Delaware 7 Sep 1987; exhibited in the airport terminal since November 1987 on loan from the Wagner Foundation which donated it outright in April 2021; live FAA registry today shows FRIENDS OF THE MITCHELL GALLERY OF FLIGHT at 5300 S Howell Ave Milwaukee valid to 31 July 2028 with MFR YEAR 1974
aliases: N1911D; c/n C3; Curtiss Model D; Curtiss Pusher E8-90

description: Taken on strength January 1945 and stored through the late 1940s at South Plains and Pyote; converted by Boeing to TB-25L then by Hughes in 1953 to TB-25M radar trainer; briefly on RCAF charge as a Mitchell IIIA1 in 1954; assigned 8 June 1958 to the 128th Consolidated Logistics and Maintenance Squadron Wisconsin ANG at General Mitchell; stricken 3 March 1960 and passed to the Air Force Museum loan programme for display at Mitchell Field on a pedestal; on loan to Milwaukee County from the National Museum of the USAF; heavily damaged in the wind and snow storm of 14-15 April 2018 when the left wing outboard of the engine collapsed without separating; displayed at the southwest corner of the airport parking structure near the base of the control tower not at the terminal gallery
